# drover

> drover runs a command as N supervised instances, load balances one public HTTP port across them, and
> replaces the binary they run with a rolling, zero-downtime rollout that can be rolled back. One static
> Linux binary, no root needed. This file is the complete reference; `drover llms` prints it.

## Model

- An **app** has a name, a command, a public `listen` address and N **instances**.
- Each instance is one process on its own loopback port (`port_base`, `port_base+1`, ...). drover restarts it
  when it exits (delay 1s, doubling to 30s).
- The load balancer on `listen` sends each request to the healthy instance with the fewest open requests.
- A **version** is a stored copy of the app's binary with a name you choose. `builtin` is the binary that
  was already on disk. Exactly one version is **current**; drover also remembers the **previous** one.
- A **rollout** switches versions one instance at a time: start the new instance on a spare port, wait until
  it is healthy, give it the slot, let the old one finish open requests (`drain_timeout`), stop it. If a new
  instance does not become healthy, the rollout is undone and the old version stays current.

## Start the server

```sh
# one app, flags only. Everything after -- is the app's command.
drover run --listen :8080 --instances 2 --health /health -- /usr/local/bin/app --port '{port}'

# config file (several apps, timeouts, env)
drover run -c drover.yaml
```

Flags for `drover run` without `-c`: `--name app` `--listen :8080` `--instances 2` `--port-base 9000`
`--health ""`. With or without `-c`: `--admin 127.0.0.1:9100` `--data <dir>` `--metrics <addr>`. Config path may also come from
`DROVER_CONFIG`, else `./drover.yaml`, else `/etc/drover.yaml`. The admin address may also come from
`DROVER_ADMIN_LISTEN` (order: `--admin`, then the variable, then the config file).

drover runs in the foreground and logs to stdout. Instance output is prefixed `[app#0]`. SIGTERM or SIGINT
stops every instance, then drover.

### Writing the command

- `{port}` → the instance's port. Also exported as `$PORT`. `{index}` → instance number from 0. `{bin}` →
  path of the binary of the version the instance runs.
- If the command has no `{bin}`, its first word is the binary that versions replace.
- No shell runs the command: no `VAR=x cmd`, pipes, `&&`, globbing or `$VAR` expansion. Set variables with
  `env:` in the config. Need a shell? Use `sh -c '...'` as the command and set `binary:` yourself.
- In a shell, quote `'{port}'`.
- The app must listen on 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0 at that port, speak HTTP/1.1, and must not take a fixed port
  from anywhere else (an env file that sets PORT makes all instances collide and crash-loop).
- Instances also get `DROVER_APP`, `DROVER_INDEX`, `DROVER_VERSION`. They do not get `DROVER_TOKEN`.

| Before | With drover |
|---|---|
| `myapp --port 3000` | `drover run --listen :3000 -- myapp --port '{port}'` |
| `PORT=3000 myapp --env /etc/myapp.env` | `drover run --listen :3000 -- myapp --env /etc/myapp.env` |
| `node /srv/server.js` (reads $PORT) | config: `command: node {bin}`, `binary: /srv/server.js` |

### Config file

Only `name`, `command`, `listen` are required. Unknown keys are an error. Values shown are the defaults.

```yaml
data: /home/app/.local/share/drover   # default $HOME/.local/share/drover; env DROVER_DATA; no ~ expansion
admin:
  listen: 127.0.0.1:9100              # flag --admin or env DROVER_ADMIN_LISTEN win
  token: ""                           # env DROVER_TOKEN wins. Required when listen is not loopback.
image_fetch_url: ""                   # env DROVER_IMAGE_FETCH_URL. Needed only for image sources.
max_binary_bytes: 1073741824
log_lines: 1000                       # recent lines kept in memory per app for the logs endpoint
metrics:
  listen: ""                          # e.g. ":9101": extra listener serving only /metrics, no token
apps:
  - name: web                         # letters, digits, . _ -  (max 64)
    command: /usr/local/bin/web --port {port}   # string or YAML list
    binary: ""                        # default: first word of command
    listen: ":8080"
    instances: 1                      # (the --instances flag defaults to 2)
    port_base: 9000                   # uses port_base .. port_base+2*instances-1; apps must not overlap
    health:
      path: ""                        # GET, 2xx/3xx = healthy. Empty = TCP connect to the port.
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
    start_timeout: 30s                # a new instance must be healthy within this or the rollout is undone
    drain_timeout: 30s                # how long an old instance may finish open requests / WebSockets
    stop_timeout: 10s                 # after stop_signal, time until SIGKILL
    stop_signal: TERM                 # TERM INT QUIT HUP KILL USR1 USR2
    try_duration: 5s                  # how long a request waits for a healthy instance before 503
    dir: ""                           # working directory
    env: {}                           # extra environment variables
```

## Control a running drover

Client commands talk to the admin API at `DROVER_ADMIN` (a URL, default `http://127.0.0.1:9100`; set it
when the server's address was changed, it does not follow `DROVER_ADMIN_LISTEN`) and send
`DROVER_TOKEN` when set. They print the JSON response and exit 0, or print the error to stderr and exit 1.
Positional arguments come before flags. Commands that roll out block until the rollout is over.

| Goal | CLI | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Status of all apps | `drover status` | `GET /apps` |
| Status of one app | `drover status <app>` | `GET /apps/<app>` |
| List versions | `drover releases <app>` | `GET /apps/<app>/releases` |
| Read app output | `drover logs <app> [-f] [--tail n] [--instance n]` | `GET /apps/<app>/logs?tail=n&instance=n&follow=true` |
| Prometheus metrics | `drover metrics` | `GET /metrics` |
| Add a version from a file | `drover upload <app> <file> --version <v>` | `PUT /apps/<app>/releases/<v>` (body = the file; `curl -T file URL`) |
| Add a version from a URL | `drover fetch <app> --url <url> --version <v>` | `POST /apps/<app>/releases` `{"url":"...","version":"v"}` |
| Add a version from a container image | `drover fetch <app> --image <ref> --path </file> --version <v>` | `POST /apps/<app>/releases` `{"image":"...","path":"...","version":"v"}` |
| Switch to a version | `drover activate <app> <v>` | `POST /apps/<app>/releases/<v>/activate` |
| Switch to the previous version | `drover rollback <app>` | `POST /apps/<app>/rollback` |
| Rolling restart, same version | `drover restart <app>` | `POST /apps/<app>/restart` |
| Delete a version | `drover rm <app> <v>` | `DELETE /apps/<app>/releases/<v>` |
| Is drover up (no token needed) | | `GET /healthz` |

Adding a version also switches to it. To only store it: `--no-activate`, `"activate": false`, or
`?activate=false` on the PUT. Optional checksum: `--sha256 <hex>`, `"sha256"`, or `?sha256=`. Without a
version name, fetch and `drover upload` use a UTC timestamp like `20261116-154400`. Private image:
`--username`/`--password` or `"username"`/`"password"`. Version names: letters, digits, `.` `_` `-`, max 64,
not `builtin`. A name cannot be reused; delete it first.

### Logs

Plain text, one line per line of output, oldest first: `<RFC3339 time> [<app>#<instance>] <line>`. Lines
without `#<instance>` are drover's own events about the app (rollouts, exits). Default `tail` is 200; the
buffer holds the last `log_lines` (1000) per app, stdout and stderr merged, and is empty after drover
restarts. `follow=true` keeps the response open (`curl -N`). Full history is in drover's stdout
(`docker logs`), where the same lines appear as `[app#0] line`.

### Metrics

Prometheus text format at `GET /metrics` on the admin API (token applies) and, when `metrics.listen` or
`--metrics` is set, on that address without a token. Series: `drover_requests_total{app,code}`,
`drover_request_duration_seconds{app}` (histogram), `drover_retries_total{app}`,
`drover_instance_exits_total{app}`, `drover_rollouts_total{app,result="success"|"failed"}`,
`drover_instances{app}`, `drover_healthy_instances{app}`, `drover_inflight_requests{app,instance}`,
`drover_rollout_in_progress{app}`, `drover_version_info{app,version}`, `drover_build_info{version}`.
Code `499` = client went away, `101` = upgraded connection. Counters reset when drover restarts.

### Responses

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Done. Body is the app status (or the list). |
| 201 | Version stored, not activated. Body is the release. |
| 204 | Deleted. |
| 400 | Bad request: invalid version name, bad JSON, empty or too large binary, sha256 mismatch. |
| 401 | Missing or wrong token. Send `X-Drover-Token: <token>` (use this behind a proxy that owns `Authorization`) or `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. If `X-Drover-Token` is present, only it is checked. |
| 404 | No such app or version. |
| 409 | Version name already exists; another rollout of this app is running; no previous version to roll back to; tried to delete the current version or `builtin`. |
| 500 | Rollout failed and was undone. The app is still on the version from before. A version that was just added stays stored. When the new binary exited, the message ends with its last output lines. |
| 502 | drover could not download the URL or image file. Nothing was stored. |

Errors are `{"message": "..."}`.

Status body:

```json
{"name":"web","listen":"[::]:8080","version":"v2","previous":"v1","rolling":false,
 "instances":[{"slot":0,"port":9000,"pid":123,"version":"v2","state":"healthy","inflight":0,"restarts":0,
               "started":"2026-11-16T15:44:00Z"}]}
```

Instance `state`: `healthy` (gets traffic), `unhealthy` (running, failing its check), `down` (exited, waiting
to restart), `draining` (old instance finishing requests), `empty` (no binary to run yet). `restarts` counts
exits of that instance since it was started.

Release entry: `{"version","size","sha256","source","created","current"}`.

## Recipes

Deploy a new build and confirm it:

```sh
drover upload web ./build/web --version "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" || echo "rollout failed, old version still serving"
drover status web          # every instance: "state":"healthy", "version": the new one
drover logs web --tail 20  # what the new instances printed
```

Roll back: `drover rollback web`. To a specific one: `drover releases web`, then `drover activate web <v>`.

Start with no binary and deploy later: use `command: "{bin} --port {port}"` with no `binary:`. Requests get
503 until the first `drover upload`.

In a Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
COPY --from=ghcr.io/mrofi/drover:latest /drover /usr/local/bin/drover
USER 1000
CMD ["drover", "run", "--listen", ":8080", "--instances", "3", "--", "app", "--port", "{port}"]
```

Read-only root filesystem: set `DROVER_DATA` to a writable mount that allows execution.

## Diagnose

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| 503 `no healthy instance` | No instance is healthy. `drover status <app>`, then `drover logs <app>`. |
| Instances `down`, `restarts` climbing | The command exits. Usual causes: wrong flag, `{port}` unquoted in a shell, a fixed port so instances collide, binary not executable or built for another libc/arch. |
| Instances `unhealthy` | Process runs but `health.path` does not return 2xx/3xx, or it listens on another interface or port. |
| Upload returns 500 `keeps exiting right after start` | The new binary crashes on start. Old version still serves. The reason is in the error (`its last output:`) and in `drover logs <app>`. Fix the build; `drover rm <app> <v>` removes the bad one. |
| Upload returns 500 `not healthy after ...` | The new binary starts too slowly or fails its health check. Raise `start_timeout` or fix the check. |
| 409 on upload | That version name exists. Pick another or delete it. |
| 502 `upstream error` | The instance accepted the request, then failed. Such a request is not retried. |
| drover refuses to start: `not loopback` | `admin.listen` is on the network without a token. Set `DROVER_TOKEN`. |
| `address already in use` at start | Something else has the `listen` or admin port. |
| Version back to `builtin` after a container restart | The data directory is not on a volume. |

## Limits

- HTTP/1.1 to instances only. No TLS, no raw TCP, no sticky sessions.
- WebSockets work. A rollout closes connections still open on an old instance after `drain_timeout`;
  clients must reconnect.
- The instance count cannot change while running: change the config and restart drover.
- Version names are fixed; there are no movable aliases such as `stable`.
- The admin API can replace running binaries. Keep it on loopback or behind a token.
- Do not stop or restart the `drover` process to deploy; use the commands above.
